question: Combined oral contraceptive pills (COCPs) are absolutely contraindicated in which clinical situation?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Mild dysmenorrhoea is actually one of the non-contraceptive therapeutic uses of COCPs. There is no contraindication here.
Correct! Combined OCP + smoking (especially >35 years or >15 cigarettes/day) creates a synergistic risk of arterial thromboembolism (MI, stroke). This is a WHO category 4 absolute contraindication.
Acne is a recognised non-contraceptive benefit of COCPs (anti-androgenic progestogens). No contraindication in a healthy patient.

answers.text: Irregular menstrual cycles in a 20-year-old with no comorbidities

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: COCPs are often prescribed to regulate menstrual cycles. There is no contraindication in a healthy young woman without risk factors.

overallFeedback.feedback: COCPs are absolutely contraindicated in heavy smokers aged >35, patients with a personal history of VTE, migraine with aura, uncontrolled hypertension, or oestrogen-sensitive cancers.
Correct! The oestrogen-smoking combination multiplies thrombotic risk, making this an absolute (WHO category 4) contraindication.
